about.title: Clayton Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Clayton is a small, close-knit city tucked against Mount Diablo, but defective products don't discriminate by zip code — a malfunctioning tool used on a Keller Ridge Drive job site, a faulty appliance in a home near downtown, or a mislabeled product picked up at a local store can all cause serious harm. California generally applies strict liability to these cases, meaning an injured person typically doesn't have to prove the manufacturer was careless — only that the product was defective and that the defect caused the injury. That can apply to design flaws, manufacturing errors, or inadequate warnings. Liability can extend beyond the manufacturer to distributors and retailers who put the product into the marketplace. If you were hurt by something that malfunctioned, broke, or failed to warn you of a hidden danger, contact us for a free case review to understand your options.

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify Your Case
items.desc: Because California often applies strict liability to defective products, you may not need to prove the manufacturer acted carelessly — just that the defect caused your injury.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable, which may widen the path to recovering compensation.

items.title: Guidance on Preserving Evidence
items.desc: Our team can advise you on keeping the product itself intact, since it's often the most important evidence in a design, manufacturing, or warning-defect claim.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California product liability claims often rely on strict liability, meaning you generally just need to show the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury. We can review the specifics of what happened to you.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Try to keep it exactly as it was at the time of the incident, including any packaging, instructions, or remaining pieces. Don't attempt repairs or discard it, since the product itself is often central evidence in these claims.

items.question: Are product injuries common around Clayton?
items.answer: Clayton is a small city, and most public crash data centers on roads like Clayton Road and Marsh Creek Road rather than product incidents. Still, defective products can injure people anywhere — at home, at work, or out shopping — and a free consultation can help clarify whether you have a claim.

items.question: Is there a cost to speak with an attorney?
items.answer: No. Our team works on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation.
